turns.doctor_question: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Hi. Honestly, I'm mostly here because HR at work and my sister keep saying I've gotten too thin. I don't really see it that way, though. From my side, I just see that my suits fit a lot sharper for my sales calls. My weight has kept dropping since my divorce, but... yeah, they're the ones who really pushed me to come in and see someone.

symptom_reasoning.S044: The patient reports continuous weight loss since his divorce, acknowledging that his weight has kept dropping to the extent that family and coworkers are concerned he has gotten too thin.

turns.doctor_question: When you look at yourself in the mirror or think about your body, do you feel afraid of gaining weight or see yourself as needing to be thinner, even though others say you're too thin?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I guess I do have a fear of gaining it back. I don't necessarily look in the mirror and think I need to be a lot thinner, but... if the scale is even a pound higher after a client dinner, or maybe a weekend out in Miami, I get this sudden panic. It just feels like I'm losing control. As soon as I see that number, I immediately start planning how I'm going to cut back the next day to fix it.

symptom_reasoning.S045: The patient explicitly confirms experiencing a fear of gaining weight, describing sudden panic and feeling a loss of control when the scale increases by even a pound.

turns.doctor_question: When you feel you need to 'cut back' after seeing a higher number on the scale, do you ever also have episodes where you eat a large amount of food and feel you can't control it, followed by things like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising excessively to make up for it?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't really do anything like that. I don't have times where I eat a huge amount of food and feel out of control, so I don't do the other stuff either—like making myself throw up or taking laxatives. When I say I cut back, I just mean I restrict what I eat the next day. I'll skip meals or just eat very little to get the number back down. But I don't have those bingeing episodes you're talking about.

symptom_reasoning.S043: The patient explicitly confirms restricting their food intake by skipping meals and eating very little to reduce their weight.
symptom_reasoning.S048: The patient clearly denies engaging in purging behaviors such as self-induced vomiting or using laxatives.
symptom_reasoning.S049: The patient explicitly denies having episodes of eating a huge amount of food.
symptom_reasoning.S050: The patient explicitly denies experiencing a feeling of being out of control while eating.

turns.doctor_question: Since your divorce, have you been feeling persistently sad, down, or losing interest and pleasure in things you used to enjoy, most of the day, nearly every day?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. I mean, the divorce was tough, obviously, but I wouldn't say I've been feeling sad or down all the time. I still go out, I still enjoy my job and hitting my sales targets, and I still like hanging out with my friends or traveling. I haven't really lost interest in my life or anything like that. I'm just very focused on my routine right now.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient explicitly denies feeling persistently sad or down all the time.
symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient states that they still enjoy their work and social activities, explicitly denying having lost interest in life.

turns.doctor_question: Can you tell me your current height and weight, so I can get a sense of where you stand in terms of body weight?
turns.patient_response: I'm about 5'10", and I think I'm around 115 pounds right now. Honestly, the only reason I'm even talking to you is because HR at work and my sister keep getting on my case, saying I've gotten too thin. But from my side... I just see that my suits fit sharper. The weight has just kept dropping since the divorce, and I don't really see it as the problem they think it is.

symptom_reasoning.S044: The patient reports a height of 5'10" and a weight of 115 lbs (significantly low BMI) and notes that their weight has continued to drop.
symptom_reasoning.S084: The patient dismisses external concerns about being too thin and states they do not see their low weight as a problem, demonstrating a lack of recognition of the seriousness of their low weight.
